title: kith-jmap + kithd: expose ownerUserId and ownerLogin in Session
description:
The JMAP session at /.well-known/jmap currently exposes 'username' (the caller's display name), but NOT the server owner's Tailscale user ID. A peer probing this endpoint cannot identify whose kithd it is. Add ownerUserId and ownerLogin to the Session struct so discovery works.

What: Two small changes — one in kith-jmap (add fields to Session struct), one in kithd (populate those fields from AppState).

Algorithm:
1. In kith-jmap/src/lib.rs, add to Session struct:
   - owner_user_id: String  (serde rename: ownerUserId)
   - owner_login: String    (serde rename: ownerLogin)

2. In kithd, the session_handler calls build_session(). Find where build_session is called and what parameters it receives. The AppState must have the owner's user_id and login_name available (from startup — kithd queries WhoIs/status on boot and stores in AppState or the 'self' table).

3. Read AppState to find owner_id (already present for authorization checks). Also need owner_login_name. If AppState only has owner_id, read the self table or add owner_login to AppState at startup.

4. Pass owner_user_id and owner_login into build_session() and set the new Session fields.

5. Tests:
   - Test: build a Session with owner_user_id='uid-alice' and owner_login='alice@example.com'; serialize to JSON; assert ownerUserId and ownerLogin appear in output.
   - Test: parse a JSON session with ownerUserId and ownerLogin; assert deserialization works.

Defensive programming rules:
- These fields are read-only (never trust them from incoming requests)
- owner_user_id and owner_login are from LocalAPI WhoIs (trusted) at startup
- Do not log owner_user_id in any error path
